title: Baci di Alassio
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Delicate hazelnut and chocolate meringue-style cookies from the Ligurian coastal town of Alassio, two domed halves sandwiched together with a rich chocolate ganache.
longDesc: Similar in spirit to Piedmont's baci di dama but built on a lighter, meringue-based hazelnut cookie rather than a buttery shortbread, these cookies have been a signature of Alassio's pasticcerie since the early 20th century.
ingredients: 200 g (1 1/3 cups) hazelnuts, toasted and finely ground
120 g (4.2 oz) dark chocolate, melted, for the filling
40 g (3 tbsp) unsalted butter, softened, for the filling
steps: Combine the ground hazelnuts, sugar, egg whites, and cocoa powder into a smooth, thick paste.
Pipe or spoon small, even domes of the mixture onto a lined baking sheet, spacing them apart.
Bake at 150C (300F) for 12-15 minutes until just set but still soft inside.
Cool completely on the tray, as the cookies are delicate while warm.
Combine the melted chocolate and softened butter into a smooth ganache.
Spread a small amount of ganache on the flat side of one cookie and press a matching cookie on top to sandwich.
Let the ganache set before serving.
chefTips: Grind the hazelnuts as finely as possible for the smoothest cookie texture.
Keep the domes small and evenly sized so they pair up neatly once sandwiched.
Let the cookies cool completely before handling, as they are quite delicate while still warm.
commonMistakes: Over-baking, which dries out the cookies and loses their intended soft, slightly chewy center.
Handling the warm cookies too soon, causing them to break.
Using too much filling, which can make the delicate cookies difficult to bite through neatly.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
healthBenefits: Hazelnuts provide healthy fats, vitamin E, and some fiber.
culturalNote: Baci di Alassio have been a signature specialty of the Ligurian coastal town of Alassio since the early 20th century, distinct from Piedmont's similar baci di dama in their lighter, meringue-based texture.
